plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors, since your payment depends only on the second-highest bid, not your own bid (as long as you win). Bidding above or below your value only risks either winning at a loss or missing profitable wins. Therefore, the optimal strategy is straightforward: bid exactly my valuation of $27 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy since you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid. This holds regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win against a bid between my value and my bid. Underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $15 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of other bidders' behavior. Since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. I'll bid my true value of $33.
